blurb:
Fourteen years old and still going strong. Ronnie is a 13-pound domestic shorthair who has been around long enough to know exactly what he wants: people, other pets, and a place to just exist without drama. He's calm, he's sweet, and he gets along with other animals without any of the territorial nonsense you sometimes get with cats.

He doesn't have a documented history with kids, but the shelter staff think he'd do just fine. A cat this easygoing for this long tends to roll with most situations. If you've got a quiet house or a home with other pets looking for a low-maintenance companion, Ronnie fits.

Senior cats get overlooked constantly. That's just the reality. But a cat this age is done with the chaos phase. He's not going to knock things off your counter at 3am for fun. He's going to find a warm spot, purr, and appreciate the fact that someone gave him a second chapter.

Ronnie is vaccinated, microchipped, flea-treated, and neutered. Walk in during visiting hours and ask to spend some time with him. He's the kind of cat who makes the decision easy.
shelter_hours: Contact shelter for current visiting hours
scoring_notes:
• Senior cat with a heartfelt narrative that will resonate deeply with readers seeking a low-drama companion
• The '3am counter-knocking' line is newsletter gold — punchy, relatable, and shareable
• 14-year-old cats are statistically the hardest to place, making his feature both urgent and emotionally compelling

blurb:
Eleven years old and still has a spring in his step. That's Meeko. He's a 33-pound Jack Russell Terrier and Greyhound mix who came out of animal control and has been soaking up love from volunteers and his foster family ever since.

He's a lap dog with real personality behind it. He'll climb right into your lap if you sit still long enough, and he's not shy about letting you know when he wants attention. He's vocal. His foster home is a house, not a condo or apartment, and that's probably the right fit for him going forward. During his shelter bath, he let out what the staff described as grateful sighs of appreciation. That tells you everything you need to know about this guy.

Meeko wants to be your only dog. He's not interested in sharing the house with another pup, and he's shown some prey drive around small animals, so cats are a question mark. He was a little nervous around younger kids, so a quieter home with teens or adults would suit him best.

He's currently in a foster home and ready to meet the right person. Contact Mostly Mutts through their website or by phone to set up a meet.
shelter_hours: See mostlymutts.org for current hours and adoption appointments
scoring_notes:
• The 'grateful sighs' bath moment is the kind of specific, human detail that makes readers stop scrolling and feel something
• At 11 years old from animal control with multiple household restrictions, he's a harder placement — urgency is high and real
• Lap dog with big personality in a senior package appeals directly to the empty-nester and retiree segment of newsletter readers

blurb:
Victor's foster turns the TV on for him when he leaves the house. That detail alone should tell you what kind of dog we're dealing with here.

He's a five-year-old Bulldog mix, about 44 pounds, and his whole body wags when something excites him. Not just the tail. The whole body. He went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program and came out of it a well-mannered, affectionate dog who the volunteers straight up call a super sweet boy. He's calm at bath time, soaks up one-on-one attention, and has been described as having the most beautiful eyes, which, fair.

He's got some energy and can get mouthy when he's excited, so kids 15 and up are a better fit, and he'd do best as your only dog since he's not a fan of other pups. He's also working through some leg challenges right now with support from his foster, so his full medical picture is worth asking about when you reach out. He's handling it like a champ.

If you want a dog who's going to be genuinely thrilled every single time you walk in the door, Victor is your guy. Reach out to Mostly Mutts through their website or by phone to learn more and set up a meeting.

blurb:
Bolton came into Mostly Mutts underweight, with thin fur, and no real history anyone knows about. That was then. Now he's 64 pounds of happy hound mix who lights up every room he walks into, which is apparently how his foster describes him, and honestly it tracks.

He went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program and learned a lot. He knows how to be around people, he loves sniffing everything on a walk, and he's got this signature move where he runs toward another dog and then bolts the other direction, hoping they'll chase him. It's goofy. It's very Bolton. He's equally happy to just hang out and relax with you when the mood calls for it.

At nine years old, he's not looking for a marathon training partner. He wants a calm, loving home where he can be a loyal companion. No cats, please. He'll chase them. Kids around 8 to 12 have been a great fit in his foster home, and he does well with dog-friendly dogs too. Toddlers might get accidentally bumped over just from his size and enthusiasm, so keep that in mind.

Bolton is currently in a foster home and doing great. To meet him, reach out to Mostly Mutts directly through their website or give them a call.
shelter_hours: See mostlymutts.org for current hours and adoption appointments
scoring_notes:
• Underweight rescue to 64-pound, Prison Pups-trained companion is a powerful transformation story with real reader pull
• Goofy chase-me personality detail is instantly memorable and gives the blurb a viral-worthy moment
• Senior dog who came in with no history and still hasn't found a home signals meaningful wait time and adoption urgency

blurb:
Pumps is about two and a half months old, roughly two pounds, and named after a shoe — because Mostly Mutts is running a shoe-themed kitten group right now and honestly that's pretty great. She was born into the rescue program, went straight to a foster home, and has been growing up well. She just moved into the Kitty Room at the shelter, which means she's ready to meet people.

Her foster is upfront about one thing: Pumps is the shyest of her siblings. She's not going to rush over and climb on you the first time you meet. She'll find a safe spot, watch what's going on, and take her time deciding you're trustworthy. But she's also genuinely curious — she wants to know what's happening, she just needs to figure it out on her own terms. Give her that space and she turns into a playful, energetic kitten who loves chasing toys, wrestling, and climbing anything she can reach. She's litter trained and does well with other cats. She'd be a great fit for a household with older kids who know how to be calm around animals, and she'd probably love having another cat to play with.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Stop by the Kitty Room to meet Pumps or visit mostlymutts.org to start the process.

scoring_notes:
• Shoe-themed litter is a fun, shareable newsletter detail that draws casual readers in with a smile
• Playful kitten energy with a shy twist appeals to readers who love a little project with a big payoff

blurb:
She came into Mostly Mutts through a tough situation — a family member passed away, a good neighbor stepped in to help, and somehow this little tuxedo cat ended up pregnant on top of everything else. She had her four kittens in a foster home, raised them well, and now most of them have already found homes. Boots is ready to find one too.

She's about three years old, roughly six pounds, and very much her own person. She's not going to follow you around the house begging for attention. But when she decides it's time for company, she'll come find you — lap, pets, treats, whatever she's in the mood for. Her foster has her figured out and says once you learn her style, she's a great companion. She does have one thing worth knowing: if you pet her past her limit, she'll give you a little nip to let you know she's done. Not aggressive, just communicative. Adults who can read a cat and respect her signals will get along with her just fine. She's good with other cats and would likely enjoy a calm housemate.

Mostly Mutts is located in Kennesaw. You can browse available cats in their Kitty Room during shelter hours or reach out through their website to start the process.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Touching origin story — loss, rescue, motherhood — gives readers an immediate emotional hook
• Best suited for experienced cat owners who can read feline cues, narrowing but not eliminating her audience
• Kittens already adopted while mom waits creates quiet urgency that newsletter readers will feel

blurb:
Bernadette is one year old and has already had a full life. She ended up outside at a young age, had kittens of her own, and was found in a family's backyard with her whole litter. They brought everyone inside, kept them safe, and almost all her kittens are now in homes. Now it's her turn.

She's about seven and a half pounds, litter trained, and her foster describes her as a cat with a gentle soul and a lot of love to give. That tracks with everything else in her profile. She's a little shy at first — she needs a minute to settle in and feel safe before she opens up. But once she trusts you, she leans in. Head bumps, asking for pets, curling up in your lap for long stretches. She's been great with kids in her foster home and gets along well with other cats too. If you have a calm household and a little patience for the first week or two, she's going to be exactly the cat you were hoping for.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Visit their website to see Bernadette in the Kitty Room or submit an inquiry to get the adoption process started.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Kid-friendly, cat-friendly, and affectionate once settled — broad household appeal with low barriers to adoption
• Stray-to-mother-to-foster arc is relatable and redemptive, exactly the kind of story newsletter readers share
• Young age combined with outdoor survival backstory makes her stand out as a resilient, rewarding companion

blurb:
Bolton came into rescue underweight, with thin fur, and a past nobody could piece together. That was then. Classic tag energy. He's equally happy to just hang out and sniff around the yard, because hound brain never fully clocks out.

Kids around 8 to 12 are actually a great match, and he's been friendly with other dogs in his foster home. He'd love a household with another playful dog to entertain him.

blurb:
Pumps is about ten weeks old, around two pounds, and part of a shoe-themed litter that was born right inside the Mostly Mutts program. She went straight to a foster home, grew up there, and just moved into the shelter's Kitty Room. She's ready.

She's the shyest of her siblings, which her foster is pretty upfront about. She'll hang back when she first meets you, find a good observation spot, and watch until she figures out the situation. She's not scared so much as deliberate. But she's also incredibly curious and can't resist knowing what's happening around her, so she won't stay in the background for long.

Once she's comfortable, she turns into a full-on adventure kitten. Chasing toys, wrestling, climbing anything she can reach, finding the highest lookout spot in the room. She's already litter trained and loves having other cats around, so a home with a resident kitty would be a great fit. Because she's on the shyer side and doesn't love being startled or handled roughly, older kids would be a better match than little ones.

If you've got patience and a calm home, she'll grow into a genuinely devoted companion. Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Stop by the Kitty Room to meet her.
scoring_notes:

blurb:
At one year old, Bernadette has already lived more life than most cats twice her age. She ended up outside too young, had a litter of kittens, and got found by a foster family who spotted her in their backyard and brought her whole family inside. Her kittens are almost all placed now. She's been patient. Now it's her turn.

She's about seven and a half pounds and has a playful streak she hasn't fully outgrown yet. Feather wands, batting toys around, that kind of thing.

She is a little shy when she first meets someone new. Not scared, just cautious. Give her a little time to get comfortable and she flips completely. Head bumps, asking to be petted, settling into your lap for hours. She's not a cat who warms up halfway. Once she trusts you, she's all in.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Visit her profile online or stop by to meet her in person.
scoring_notes:

blurb:

Her foster figured it out fast and says it's a total non-issue once you learn her signals. Because of that, she'd do best with adults or older kids who can pick up on the cues and respect them. She gets along with other cats, so if you've got one at home, that could work well too.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. You can browse her full profile on their website and reach out to get the adoption process started.
